transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SA), Ravi Patel (Aerialis VP Platform), Lena Novak (Aerialis ML Lead), Omar Hassan (Aerialis Security), Sofia Marin (Aerialis Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Aerialis is evaluating Redwood for telephony and agent-assist features across EN/ES/FR/AR with heavy context (32k+ tokens) and tool-calling to internal knowledge APIs.
- Main concerns: latency at peak (95p), data residency / KMS, and cost tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Agreed next steps: share security pack, pricing tiers, and run a 2-week POC with pre-defined prompts and throughput targets.

Topics: model comparison, context length, multilingual, tool-calling, deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), security (SOC2, KMS), benchmarks and POC scope.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i know we have an hour-ish, um we'll try to cover model selection and how redwood would run in your environment, does that still work for y'all?
[00:08] Ravi Patel: yeah that's perfect, we've got only like one ask up front, which is we need to understand how this behaves when we hit bursty call volume and multilingual transcripts, like spanish and arabic.
[00:17] Diego Ramos: totally, that is a common pattern. quick question — are you leaning toward hosted api first, or do you expect dedicated/reserved or private on prem?
[00:24] Lena Novak: i'd say hosted for dev, but our goal is dedicated or private for production because of compliance and low-latency to our internal voice stack.
[00:33] Sofia Marin: and just to add, we have intent routing that needs 30k token context for threaded conversations, so context length is a big decision for us.
[00:42] Maya Chen: ok got it, so context length, multilingual, and tool-calling. we'll walk through model families that make sense, and then runtime options — and we can map cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:52] Diego Ramos: quick note on terminology — when we say tool-calling that's function-calling / external api calls from the model, right?
[00:56] Lena Novak: yeah, we call our internal KG and a microservice for real-time presence.
[01:02] Omar Hassan: and security wise we need SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention policy controls, plus KMS with HSM-backed keys. also SOC2 type ii is required.
[01:11] Priya Kapoor: we support SSO, role-based access and detailed audit logs, and redwood private can be deployed in a VPC with customer KMS integration. we'll include SOC2 docs in the pack.
[01:20] Ravi Patel: great. on model selection — what are the open-model options that handle 30k-64k token contexts reliably without huge cost blowups?
[01:28] Diego Ramos: good question. for 30k-64k context you typically look at models trained+optimized for longer context — some LLaMA variants and certain Mistral forks, but you'll want models with chunked attention or efficient attention kernels. Redwood also supports mapping to quantized variants for cost savings.
[01:43] Lena Novak: so you're saying we could use a 32k model in hosted, but if we need 64k we might need a different variant or dedicated infra?
[01:50] Diego Ramos: yeah, for 64k you may want dedicated capacity because the memory/kv cache and sequence kernels are heavier. Dedicated lets you pin instances with more memory and throughput. Private on-prem is also viable if you have strict data residency.
[02:02] Sofia Marin: and accuracy — we care about Spanish legal-ese and Arabic dialects. which models have better multilingual grounding?
[02:09] Diego Ramos: multilingual performance varies. models like M2-xx and some BLOOMX variants do well cross-lingual, but if you have domain-specific fine-tuning (legal), we'd recommend a small fine-tune / retrieval-augmented pipeline. Redwood supports reranking and custom evals to measure regressions.
[02:23] Ravi Patel: can you run retriever + model locally in private? our legal data can't leave our VPC.
[02:29] Maya Chen: yes — Redwood Private can run entirely within your VPC or on-prem, with customer-managed storage and KMS. the control plane can be isolated and audit logs shipped to your splunk/elk.
[02:40] Omar Hassan: latency SLA question — we want 95th percentile < 150ms for short-turn queries, but threaded context responses can be allowed up to 500ms. is that realistic?
[02:49] Diego Ramos: 150ms 95p for short queries is aggressive but possible with warmed KV cache, batching disabled for low-latency routes, and using smaller faster model variants for classification. For long-context generation, 300-500ms is more realistic depending on tokens generated and model size.
[03:03] Lena Novak: what about token costs — if we run a big model with 32k context all the time that's going to be expensive. any levers?
[03:09] Priya Kapoor: batching strategies, prefix caching, and hybrid routing help — e.g., route short queries to a fast 7B variant hosted, while heavy context flows go to dedicated instances with kv cache and quantized weights to reduce memory and cost. Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles automatically from a sample workload.
[03:23] Ravi Patel: tool-calling — we have several synchronous API calls per request. will that add latency or complicate fallbacks?
[03:29] Diego Ramos: it will add coordination overhead. Redwood supports function-calling patterns with retries and timeouts, and you can configure fallbacks — like if the external microservice is slow, fall back to a cached answer or a smaller model. Also we can do prefetching patterns if your tools are predictable.
[03:43] Sofia Marin: for the POC, can we include heavy tool-calling and a multi-language set?
[03:47] Maya Chen: absolutely, that's the plan. we'll design a test harness that covers English, Spanish, Arabic, intents, and tool-call flows.
[03:52] Omar Hassan: network egress — if hosted option sends PII offsite that's non-starter. do you have an on-prem installer?
[03:59] Priya Kapoor: we do. Redwood Private includes an on-prem package that keeps inference in your network. alternatively Dedicated can be deployed in a partner region with strict data residency. we will detail network diagrams in the security pack.
[04:12] Ravi Patel: ok good. one more technical — when you say kv cache, how does that handle threaded conversation where context slides? do we keep a sparse cache or full token store?
[04:20] Diego Ramos: we maintain kv cache per session; for extremely long threads we shard the context and only materialize the parts needed via retrieval. there's also prefix caching to speed repeated prompts. it's a combination to avoid storing full sequences in memory.
[04:31] Lena Novak: are there any notable degradation risks when moving from hosted quantized models to dedicated fp16 or int8?
[04:38] Diego Ramos: quantization can introduce small quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can run differential evals against your evaluation set to quantify the change. often int8 is a sweet spot for cost with negligible perf drop, but you'll want to run tests on your prompts.
[04:50] Maya Chen: let's talk ops — who will be the internal owners on your side and what's your timeline?
[04:55] Ravi Patel: timeline is Q2 pilot start, hoping to be in production by Q3 if pilot looks good. owners are Lena for ML, Omar for security, and Ravi for platform.
[05:05] Sofia Marin: budget expectations — we have an initial pilot budget at around $40k for the two-week POC and some reserved capacity trials.
[05:12] Maya Chen: that's helpful, we'll map POC scope to that number and the options.
[05:17] Diego Ramos: ok for the POC we'll propose three tracks: 1) Hosted quickstart with fast 7B models for latency tests, 2) Dedicated with 32k context model and pinned capacity for throughput/95p latency, 3) Private VPC run with sample integration to your KMS and internal KG for retrieval.
[05:31] Lena Novak: for the dedicated track — can you simulate our peak 200 qps? we need to see sustained throughput.
[05:36] Diego Ramos: yes, we can drive a benchmark harness, but we'll need your typical distribution: avg tokens per request, percent that need tool-calling, and language split.
[05:45] Maya Chen: action items recap — we'll send the security/compliance pack, Diego will build the POC test matrix, Lena will share sample corpus, Omar will confirm KMS details, and we'll schedule the POC kickoff next week.
[05:58] Ravi Patel: sounds good. quick question — anyone else competing? we have evals going with BigCloud AI and a homegrown route.
[06:05] Maya Chen: understood. we'll include a transparent cost/latency comparison in the deck and make sure the POC shows measurable wins on your key metrics.
[06:12] Sofia Marin: ok thanks everyone. one last thing — can you include a short example of the fallback policy when the KG is down?
[06:18] Diego Ramos: yes, we'll include examples: cache-first fallback, conservative answer generation, and escalation to human agent.
[06:24] Maya Chen: great — we'll follow up by Thursday with docs. thanks all.
[06:28] End of call.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker labels automated, occasional word swaps (e.g., "kv cache" transcribed as "K V cache"), and some punctuation missing. This is a sales discovery so there's qualification, timeline, stakeholders, and explicit next steps.
